Content:
A connected region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] can be contracted to a point.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/704ab166a81e006b18ba38f85c16fc5b]

Content:
When we have a connected plane region (e.g. a region in the [MATH: xy]-plane), determining whether it's simply connected is a little simpler: we just need to check whether the region contains holes.

Content:
Plane regions containing holes are not simply connected, since some simple closed curves cannot be contracted to a point:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/42421d933a5fae7991e550465be995cd]

Content:
So, if a connected plane region does not contain any holes, then it is simply connected.

Content:
More precisely, a connected plane region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] encloses only points in [MATH: D.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A connected region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] can be contracted to a point.

A connected plane region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] encloses only points in [MATH: D.] In other words, the region does not contain any holes. Plane regions containing holes are not simply connected, since some simple closed curves cannot be contracted to a point:

With that in mind, let's examine each of the regions:

  • Region I is not simply connected. Instead, this is a connected region that contains a hole.

  • Region II is simply connected. This is a connected region that does not contain holes.

  • Region III is not simply connected. Instead, this is a region that consists of two pieces (it's not connected).

  • Region IV is simply connected. This is a connected region that does not contain holes.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and IV only."

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A connected region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] can be contracted to a point.

A connected plane region [MATH: D] is simply connected if every simple closed curve in [MATH: D] encloses only points in [MATH: D.] In other words, the region does not contain any holes. Plane regions containing holes are not simply connected, since some simple closed curves cannot be contracted to a point:

Let's now examine our regions in turn.

  • Region I is simply connected. Indeed, it is the half-plane [MATH: y \geq x.] So, it's a plane region without holes.

  • Region II is not simply connected since it's a plane region with a hole at [MATH: (0,0).]

  • Region III is not simply connected since it's a plane region with a hole. In this case, the hole contains all points on the disc [MATH: x^2+y^2 \leq 4].

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
